q: I would just put up with it if I was 30+ weeks but I’m not sure I can manage another 24 or so weeks of this!
c: 16 weeks (UK), back pain despite nightly stretches and coached gym sessions.

q: I have booked in with an Osteopath at the end of this week - fingers crossed 🤞🏻
c: Same author five days later, after replies.

q: I want my husband to be my primary support person and he feels overwhelmed at the thought. I will have midwives etc present during the birth, but I would like my husband to not feel like he is drowning during the process.
c: Asks a doula sub for book recommendations for her husband.

q: Has anyone had a baby this big? Did you opt for a c section? Or an early induction?
c: 29 weeks; told the baby is measuring above the 99th percentile on an estimate, rescan in 4 weeks.

q: I cry every day because I'm so miserable. I remember being fairly uncomfortable in my other pregnancies but this one feels so much worse. The fatigue & inability to rest is insane.
c: 42, 37 weeks with her fifth after a short interval; everything hurts.

q: Does anyone have any tips for getting through the rest of the pregnancy without hating life every day?
c: Same author, weeks from the end.

q: I am still working out (I weigh less now than I did pre first pregnancy), I am taking 5g of creatine daily, taking my pre natal supplement + dha + vitamin d, I cut out all zero soda products, I only drink a double shot of espresso, I started eating more whole foods and cut out all of my protein bars and powder supplements. But it doesn’t feel like enough. Even the thought of having ONE Coke Zero induces anxiety.
c: 8 weeks with her second; relaxed in her first pregnancy, anxious about every choice now.

q: the doctor told me to stop taking creatine. Immediately felt like shit.
c: Same author at her first appointment; she wanted an explanation.

q: Since becoming a SAHM, my family has treated me like a full time babysitter. I watch my sister’s kids (3 and 7yo) 2-3 days a week. I watch my cousins son (2yo) 1-3 days a week. I also have my own 2 year old and I’m currently 30 weeks pregnant.
c: Asks if she is selfish for wanting to stop babysitting relatives' children.

q: I help them because you have to be a villager to have a village right? I understand that babysitters and daycare are expensive
c: Same author on why she said yes.

q: He won’t allow me to put him down AT ALL during the day. He instantly starts screaming and I feel rushed and guilty trying to hurry with what I’m doing so I can pick him back up.
c: 5 weeks postpartum, breastfeeding, asks how others find time for intimacy.

q: They don’t want me to completely hide the pregnancy, but they want me to keep it from wider family and other people for as long as possible because they’re worried people will gossip, judge me, or be nosey about how quickly I got pregnant.
c: 16 weeks (UK), first baby; religious parents supportive but want the pregnancy kept quiet.

q: Other than my partner and parents, I don’t really talk about the baby with anyone, which can feel quite lonely at times. I miss that sense of community and being able to openly share such a huge life moment with the people around me.
c: Same author.

q: the sickness and exhaustion during the first trimester were hard to cover up. I’ve had to cancel plans, avoid meals and drinks with friends, and make excuses so people wouldn’t start questioning things.
c: Same author on hiding the first trimester.

q: Is there a wait time to be eligible for maternity leave benefits (e.g., need to work at PayPal for at least x months...)? Right now I'm assuming, I would have job protection but it would not be paid if I haven't worked at the company for min 12 months. Does that track?
c: Getting a job offer while pregnant (California office); asks employees about leave rules before talking to the recruiter.

q: Anything else I should be asking/ negotiating about when starting thew new job pregnant?
c: Same author.

q: I am struggling with guilt for gaining so much weight already, feeling very fat, and generally anxious that I will gain an extreme amount of weight and not be able to lose it.
c: 9.5 weeks, has long struggled with weight; gained 10 lbs since the positive test.

q: Yes, I have that and according to it, I am gaining too much weight. The same advice is everywhere. I am just feeling bad about it, that's all.
c: Same author, replying about a weight-gain chart a commenter pointed her to.

q: HR has said they’ll need to contact my dr before approving remote status before I go out on mat leave. Is this considered a reasonable accommodation for pregnancy? Maybe once I hit the 3rd trimester?
c: 24 weeks, tech job, hour commute three days a week; wants to work from home.

q: That’s how I’m feeling - in tears getting ready for work in the morning.
c: Same author replying to a commenter.

q: Work has been nothing but drama because how dare I become pregnant and curb my own productivity. One of my superiors has been completely ignoring me for weeks.
c: First-time mum at 26 weeks, covering a quitting colleague's work.

q: Read exactly zero baby books, grew up without siblings and very little family contact so I still have no idea how to even take care of a little baby.
c: Same author; zero local support system.

q: Got a bunch of baby clothes from random people, a crib, baby bathtub and changing station, plus three plushies. That's all I had the energy to buy so far.
c: Same author.

q: I'm not in shape, not glowing, not healthy, not excited, I'm just fucking miserable at the moment. I wished I could just lie down.
c: Same author.

q: I won't be on maternity leave until 6 weeks before the EDD, so if I'm lucky I will maybe have 6 weeks max to prepare for baby and I doubt that's enough.
c: Same author.

q: I’m not that hungry sometimes and I forget to eat and I know I shouldn’t forget to eat especially being pregnant but it’s hard sometimes to recognize my hungry cues.
c: 20 weeks; felt faint at the anatomy scan, told by a nurse to add protein and snacks.

q: Why did nobody tell me how extra-exhausting breastfeeding with a toddler is!
c: 7 weeks pregnant, still feeding her 22-month-old.

q: The exhaustion is so much harder than with my first pregnancy, and I’m a SAHM vs working full time with her!
c: Same author.

q: he asked me “why are you so miserable all the time” and I told him it’s because I’m pregnant and completely exhausted from taking care of the household chores, making breakfast lunch and dinner, and also get zero intimacy from him.
c: First baby; argument with her husband about intimacy during pregnancy.

q: I know that once the baby is here he is going to have to do some of these things and I’m gonna be so frustrated having to tell him to do it.
c: Same author; he does dishes when asked and suggested a his-and-hers chore whiteboard.

q: In the weeks leading up to induction, I tried everything I reasonably could to encourage labour naturally: acupuncture, chiropractor, RMT, red raspberry leaf tea, dates, pineapple, curb walking, long walks and hikes, and lots of time on the exercise ball.
c: Canada (BC), months after an induction that ended in surgery; had wanted a home birth.

q: I didn’t feel traumatized in the moment, but months later I’ve found myself feeling a lot of grief and guilt. Wondering if I gave up too easily. If I should have tried longer. If I “failed” at the birth I wanted.
c: Same author asking strangers whether she agreed to something that cost her the birth she wanted.

q: If I compare to photos with my first (now 23 months) I was this size 32 weeks pregnant. I keep getting asked if I’m having twins (even my pharmacist has questioned me).
c: 21 weeks with her second, bump much bigger than the first time.

q: I just have no idea what the realistic healing time and emotional state is like for a new mom so I don't want to set myself up for a failure or pressure myself into doing something and then feeling guilty about it later
c: Due in July with her first; wonders about a concert a month after the birth.
